risks.note: Adverse weather, water scarcity, pest and disease outbreaks and farmers shifting to more remunerative alternative crops may reduce cane availability and hit profitability. The Company has already discontinued operations at Pettavathalai, Pudukkottai and Puducherry; existing units at Nellikuppam, Pugalur, Sivagangai and Sankili remain significantly impacted by declining cane/molasses availability and, if the trend persists, their long-term financial viability may be affected. Management concedes that farmer-engagement, Clean Seed Programme, seaweed-based solutions, mechanised harvesting and R&D initiatives may not fully mitigate the structural risk in these two States.
risks.risk: Sugarcane availability — structural decline in cane acreage, especially in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh

risks.note: Sugarcane prices are determined by the Central and State Governments and are not directly aligned with prevailing sugar prices; any mismatch resulting in unviable cane pricing directly compresses Sugar Division profitability. Mitigation is limited to advocacy through ISMA and SISMA.
risks.risk: Raw material pricing — cane price is administered and decoupled from sugar prices

risks.note: Any increase in the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane without a matching increase in the Minimum Support Price for sugar adversely impacts profitability. The Company offsets partially by shifting sales to institutional and retail segments that command a premium over the trade channel and by pushing value-added products such as Amrit and jaggery.
risks.risk: Sugar price risk — FRP rises without a corresponding MSP revision

risks.note: Failure or inadequacy of monsoons, depletion of groundwater levels and deterioration in groundwater quality threaten a water-intensive crop. The Company has adopted advanced water treatment technologies (MWTS, JIVA Water Device) and commenced sensor-based autonomous irrigation to cut consumption and lift productivity.

Non-availability of migrant labour for cane harvesting can delay timely harvesting and hurt overall productivity and recovery. Mitigation relies on local labour, self-harvesting by farmers, mechanised harvesting and wider row planting to enable machine use.

Business economics of the integrated sugar industry are significantly influenced by laws and Government policies governing sugarcane and sugar availability, pricing, power tariffs, molasses availability, and ethanol production and sales; stoppage of production due to non-compliance with pollution control regulations, labour laws or other statutory requirements is a further exposure. Financial implication is flagged as negative. Mitigation is the integrated model (sugar + distillery + bagasse-based green energy), value-added products from by-products, business continuity planning, and engagement with Government through industry bodies.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk in a cyclical industry

risks.note: Unsafe practices and an inadequate work environment may create safety risks affecting employee well-being. Mitigation includes behavioural safety capability-building at all levels, a defined maturity roadmap, and a benchmarked Safety Drive with an Action Tracking System, incident reporting, inspections and structured safety observation processes.

System unavailability or failure of critical IT systems could disrupt business operations, arising from inadequate processes, cyber security vulnerabilities or insufficient backup and disaster recovery. Mitigation includes reviewed backup and disaster recovery policies, firewalls and SIEM monitoring, and periodic user training and awareness.
risks.risk: Cyber security and IT system availability

sk.overview: The nutrition and wellness industry spans micronutrient premixes, food fortification, branded wellness/clinical nutrition and therapeutic nutrition (RUTF/RUSF, MNPs). Growth is driven by rising health awareness, ageing populations, chronic-disease prevalence, e-commerce and personalised nutrition, and public-health programmes addressing malnutrition. India remains a large undernutrition market (contributing ~30% of global childhood stunting) supported by government schemes such as POSHAN Abhiyaan and ICDS. (Per CARE Analytics industry report commissioned by the issuer, updated May 6, 2026.)
